name: @swmansion/argent

tools.name: list-devices
tools.description:
List iOS simulators, Android emulators, connected physical Android devices, running Chromium apps, and Vega (Fire TV) devices in one place.
Call this at the start of a session to pick a target id ('udid' for iOS entries, 'serial' for Android/Vega entries, 'id' for Chromium) to pass to interaction tools, and to see which targets are already running.
Returns { devices, avds } where each device carries a 'platform' discriminator ('ios', 'android', 'chromium', or 'vega'); 'avds' lists Android AVDs bootable via boot-device. A Vega VVD is listed under 'devices' whether running or stopped (state 'running'/'stopped'); start a stopped one with boot-device using its 'vvdImage'.
Android entries also carry a 'kind' ('emulator' for a local AVD, 'device' for a physical phone on USB / wireless adb). Physical phones use the same interaction tools as emulators and need no boot-device (just connect the phone with USB debugging authorised).
Physical iPhones appear as iOS entries with kind 'device' (no iPads); no boot-device. State 'connected' = cabled and usable; 'paired' = not reachable over USB, never auto-bound.
TV targets are tagged with runtimeKind 'tv' (Apple TV simulators, Android TV / leanback devices). They are focus-driven, not touch-driven: use `describe` to read focus, `tv-remote` for remote presses, and `keyboard` to type, rather than the coordinate/gesture tools.
iOS simulators from an additional CoreSimulator device set (the 'ios.additionalDeviceSets' configuration, e.g. devices created by Radon IDE) are tagged with their 'deviceSet' path; the same tools drive them by udid, but they run headless (no Simulator.app window).
A foldable iOS simulator (the iPhone Duo) or Android emulator (and its AVD) has 'foldable: true'; use the `fold` tool to fold or unfold it.
Chromium apps are discovered by probing CDP debugging ports (default 9222; extend via the ARGENT_CHROMIUM_PORTS=<comma-separated-ports> env var). They must already be running with --remote-debugging-port=<port>; use boot-device with electronAppPath to launch one.
Booted/ready devices are listed first, but use a physical phone (kind 'device') only when the user asks for one. A platform is silently omitted when its CLI is not found; an empty result usually means xcode-select, Android platform-tools, or the Vega SDK is not installed.

tools.name: boot-device
tools.description:
Start an iOS simulator, launch an Android emulator, start a Vega (Fire TV) Virtual Device, or spawn an Electron app and wait until it is ready to accept interactions.
Pass exactly one of 'udid', 'avdName', 'vvdImage', or 'electronAppPath'; it picks the platform.
Use when starting a session, once you have picked a target.
Returns a tagged payload: { platform: 'ios', udid, booted, note? } or { platform: 'android', serial, avdName, booted, note? } or { platform: 'vega', serial, vvdImage, booted } or { platform: 'chromium', id, port, pid, booted } (an Electron app boots as a Chromium/CDP device).
On Android the tool hot-boots from the AVD's default_boot snapshot when usable and falls back to a slower cold boot otherwise. Vega starts the single SDK-managed VVD (~10s). If an Android/Electron boot stage fails, the tool terminates the device it spawned so the next retry starts clean.

udid.description: iOS: simulator UDID to boot (from `list-devices`).

avdName.description: Android: AVD name to launch a new emulator from (from `list-devices` → `avds[].name`).

vvdImage.description: Vega (Fire TV): VVD image to boot: the `vvdImage` of a Vega device from `list-devices` (e.g. `tv`).

bootTimeoutMs.description: Android/Vega: overall budget for the boot sequence. Default 480000 (8 min) on Android, 120000 (2 min) on Vega. Range: 30000 to 900000.

force.description: Shut down and re-boot the device even if already running. Ignored for Electron, which always spawns a fresh process.

sound.description: Android only (argent never mutes other platforms): boot the emulator with audio output enabled. Defaults to false, so several agent-driven emulators don't all play sound on the host; pass `true` when the task involves playing, hearing, or testing audio. Takes effect at boot: if the emulator is already running muted, add `force: true`. The first boot after toggling is a slower cold boot (the snapshot was saved in the other audio mode). The `boot-sound` argent flag flips this default to true.

guestVulkan.description: Android on a macOS host only: boot the emulator with guest Vulkan. Defaults to false: guest Vulkan crashes Chrome's GPU process, which breaks Chrome and Custom Tab sign-in flows. Without it apps find no Vulkan device, although the guest still lists the Vulkan features, so a Vulkan-only renderer such as WebGPU (react-native-wgpu) draws nothing; pass `true` to test one. Takes effect at boot: an emulator already running in the other mode is reused with a `note`, and `force: true` reboots it. A boot snapshot saved in the other mode can't be reused, so the first boot after toggling is a slower cold boot. The `ARGENT_EMULATOR_GUEST_VULKAN` env var flips this default to true. Ignored on other hosts and platforms.

headless.description: iOS only: boot the simulator core WITHOUT opening its GUI window (Simulator.app, or Device Hub on Xcode 27+). The device still streams via simulator-server. The `ARGENT_SIMULATOR_NO_WINDOW` env var (1/true/yes) forces this host-wide.

electronAppPath.description: Electron: path to the Electron app to launch. Either a packaged .app bundle / executable, or a project directory whose package.json points the Electron binary at the entry script.

electronPort.description: Electron-only: CDP remote-debugging port to expose. Defaults to a free port; the resulting device id is `chromium-cdp-<port>`. Range: 1024 to 65535.

electronArgs.description: Electron-only: extra CLI arguments forwarded to the Electron binary after the app path.

tools.name: launch-app
tools.description:
Open an installed app, or confirm the running renderer (Chromium).
Use when starting any app; prefer this over tapping home-screen / launcher icons. Also prepares the native-devtools injection before the app starts (iOS and Apple TV).
Returns { launched, bundleId, note?, networkCapture? }. Fails if the app is not installed on the target device (iOS / Android). On a physical iPhone this registers the app every other tool acts on; com.apple.springboard and com.apple.Spotlight register without launching. note warns when runner signing is not ready. networkCapture (Android) says whether native network capture followed the launch.
For Chromium, the app is already running behind a CDP port; this call simply refreshes the cached viewport and acknowledges the bundleId tag. To change the visible route, use `open-url`.

Common iOS bundle ids: com.apple.MobileSMS, com.apple.mobilesafari, com.apple.Preferences, com.apple.Maps, com.apple.mobileslideshow (Photos), com.apple.MobileAddressBook
Common Android packages: com.android.settings, com.android.chrome, com.google.android.apps.maps, com.google.android.gm, com.android.vending, com.google.android.dialer, com.google.android.apps.messaging

udid.description: Target device id from `list-devices` (iOS UDID, Android serial, or Chromium id).

bundleId.description: App identifier. iOS: bundle id. Android: package name from build.gradle `applicationId`. Vega (Fire TV): the interactive component app id from manifest.toml (e.g. com.example.app.main). Chromium: any tag matching the pattern.

activity.description: Android-only: fully-qualified Activity name (e.g. `.MainActivity` or `com.example/com.example.MainActivity`). If omitted, the app's default launcher activity is used.

launchArgs.description: Apple simulators and physical iPhones: arguments passed to the app process at launch, e.g. `["-FeatureFlag", "YES"]` to override UserDefaults. A running app is relaunched to apply them. The call fails, launching nothing, if terminating it does not finish within 15s on a local iOS simulator, or fails for a reason other than the app not running on a remote one.

tools.name: restart-app
tools.description:
Terminate then relaunch an app on iOS, Android, or Vega.
Use when you need a clean in-memory state without a full reinstall. The relaunch also refreshes the native-devtools injection (iOS and Apple TV).
Returns { restarted, bundleId, networkCapture? }. networkCapture (Android) says whether native network capture followed the launch. Fails if the app is not installed, on a local iOS simulator if terminating it does not finish within 15s, or on a remote simulator if terminating it fails for a reason other than the app not running.

udid.description: Target device id from `list-devices` (iOS UDID or Android serial).

bundleId.description: App identifier. iOS: bundle id. Android: package name. Vega: interactive component app id.

activity.description: Android-only: relaunch a non-launcher Activity (e.g. `.SettingsActivity` or `com.example/com.example.SettingsActivity`). If omitted, the app's default launcher activity is used.

launchArgs.description: Apple simulators and physical iPhones: arguments passed to the app process at launch, e.g. `["-FeatureFlag", "YES"]` to override UserDefaults.

tools.name: reinstall-app
tools.description:
Install or reinstall an app on the device. The previous installation (if any) is uninstalled first so app data and runtime permissions are cleared.
Use for a full reinstall after rebuilding, or to start from a clean app state.
Returns { reinstalled, bundleId }. Fails if `appPath` does not exist or is not the platform's package, or `bundleId` does not match it (not checked on Vega or a remote simulator); these checks run before anything is uninstalled. On Android it also fails, without installing, when bundleId is still on the device after the uninstall or that check fails (the app may then be gone), and on a local iOS simulator when the uninstall does not finish within 30s.

udid.description: Target device id from `list-devices` (iOS UDID or Android serial).

bundleId.description: App identifier, used to uninstall the previous installation. iOS: bundle id. Android: package name. Vega: interactive component app id (e.g. com.example.app.main).

appPath.description: Path to the app bundle. iOS: `.app` directory (e.g. ./build/.../MyApp.app). Android: `.apk` file (e.g. android/app/build/outputs/apk/debug/app-debug.apk). Vega: `.vpkg` file. Relative paths are resolved from the current working directory.

tools.name: settings-permissions
tools.description:
Grant or deny an app's runtime permission, or reset it, without navigating the system Settings UI. Use when setting up a test, before the app asks for the permission.
iOS simulator: `grant location`/`location-always` needs the app already installed (location authorization is not applied to a bundle id until the app exists). Local simulators enforce this; a remote simulator can't be checked, so install the app there first. Other services can be granted before install.
Android: changes the mapped `android.permission.*` runtime permissions (reset also best-effort clears the user-set permission flags). The app must be installed and declare them in its manifest.
Some permission changes terminate the app if it is running (system behavior on both platforms), so set permissions before launching, or relaunch after.
Returns { action, permission, bundleId, applied, skipped? }: `applied` lists the platform-level services/permissions actually changed; `skipped` (Android) lists mapped permissions the package manager rejected, e.g. ones the manifest doesn't declare. Fails if nothing could be applied.

udid.description: Target device id from `list-devices` (iOS simulator UDID or Android serial).

action.description: `grant` pre-authorizes the permission, `deny` refuses it, `reset` returns it to the not-yet-asked state so the app prompts on next use.

permission.description: The permission to change. `notifications` is Android-only; `reminders` is iOS-only; `camera` works on Android, and on iOS only when the simulator's runtime models the service.

bundleId.description: App to change the permission for; every action, `reset` included, applies to this app only. iOS: bundle id (e.g. com.example.app). Android: package name.

tools.name: open-url
tools.description:
Open a URL or URL scheme on the device.
Use when navigating to a web page or deep-linking into an app. On Chromium, this navigates the primary renderer to the given URL; a URL that does not load a page, start a download or run as javascript:, such as tel:, mailto:, an unknown scheme or no scheme, fails there.
Cross-platform schemes on native devices: https://, tel:, mailto:. iOS also: messages://, settings://, maps://. Android also: geo:, plus any app-specific deep link.
An https:// link opens the native app only if that app is verified for the link's domain (Universal Links / App Links); even then, an iOS simulator may open Safari. To reliably open an installed app, use its custom scheme (scheme://path) or launch-app.
On a physical iPhone, the app that receives the URL becomes the app under automation.
Returns { opened, url, note? }. `note` explains the routing caveat when a web URL was opened on a native device. Fails if no app is registered to handle the URI (iOS/Android) or the renderer rejects the navigation (Chromium).

udid.description: Target device id from `list-devices` (iOS UDID, Android serial, or Chromium id).

url.description: URL or scheme to open (e.g. https://example.com, messages://, tel:555, geo:37.0,-122.0).

bundleId.description: Physical iOS only: the app that receives the URL. Defaults to Safari for http(s); required for any other scheme.

tools.name: screenshot
tools.description:
Capture a PNG of the device screen (iOS simulator or physical device, Android emulator, Apple TV simulator, Vega, or Chromium app). Returns { image }, the PNG file.
Use when you need a baseline image before an interaction or the screen state after a delay. Gestures, key presses and app launches already attach a screenshot to their result.
Fails if the capture backend (simulator-server, emulator, Chromium CDP) cannot be reached for this device.

udid.description: Target device id from `list-devices` (iOS UDID, Android serial, Apple TV UDID, Vega serial, or Chromium id).

rotation.description: Orientation override for the screenshot (on Chromium it rotates the captured image). On Android the capture already follows the device's rotation. Ignored on physical iPhones.

scale.description: Scale factor. Defaults to ARGENT_SCREENSHOT_SCALE env var, or 0.25 if unset for iOS/Android. On a local Apple TV simulator, an Android TV or Vega, with neither set, the capture is downscaled to a 576 px long side (0.15 of a 4K capture). On Chromium the default is 1.0 (no downscale); pass <1 to opt in. Downscaling on Chromium requires the optional `sharp` dependency. Range: 0.01 to 1.

includeImageInContext.description: Set false only when capturing a full-resolution PNG (scale: 1.0) to save as a baseline/current for screenshot-diff. The file is still written, but the image bytes are not attached to the agent context. Default: true.

downscaler.description: Downscaling algorithm when scale<1 on Chromium. Defaults to lanczos3 (highest quality). Ignored on every other platform.

tools.name: screenshot-diff
tools.description:
Compare two PNG screenshots and return a compact visual-diff summary.
Each side is a saved PNG or a live capture from the device. baselinePath + captureCurrent is the common visual-regression flow.
Use when stable before/after screenshots exist and the expected result is pixel-visible: layout, spacing, color, typography, image/icon rendering, clipping, overflow, or text rendering.
Physical iPhones: live captures are device-wide and need no registered app. Keep baselines per device model; different aspect ratios fail as a dimension mismatch.
Returns { summary, diffPath, contextDiffPath }. The summary uses normalized [0,1] screen locations matching describe coordinates; diffPath is the full-size diff image and contextDiffPath is a downscaled image for MCP/agent display.
Ignores the fixed top status-bar band for both pixel and OCR text comparisons.
Fails if the input sources are invalid, PNG files cannot be read, outputDir cannot be written, or the simulator-server / emulator backend is not reachable.

baselinePath.description: Path to the saved baseline PNG file. Required unless captureBaseline is true; do not pass both.

currentPath.description: Path to the saved current PNG file. Required unless captureCurrent is true; do not pass both.

udid.description: Target device id from `list-devices` (iOS UDID or Android serial).

captureBaseline.description: Capture the baseline screenshot live from the device, at full resolution, before diffing. Cannot be combined with captureCurrent.

captureCurrent.description: Capture the current screenshot live from the device, at full resolution, before diffing. Cannot be combined with captureBaseline.

rotation.description: Orientation override for live baseline/current captures. Ignored on physical iPhones.

outputDir.description: Directory where diff artifacts should be written (default: a temp directory). The diff images are returned in the result either way.

tools.name: screen-recording-start
tools.description:
Start recording the device screen to a video file (h264 mp4, 30fps at the device's native resolution).
The recording keeps running across other tool calls (every result carries a reminder) until `screen-recording-stop` is called or timeLimitSeconds elapses. Immediately after starting, set yourself a reminder/wakeup for the expected end of the recording so it is never left running.
Use when the user wants a video of an interaction, animation, or app behavior; for a single still frame use `screenshot` instead.
Returns { status: "recording", timeLimitSeconds, outputFile }. The video is retrieved later by `screen-recording-stop`, not by reading outputFile directly.
Fails if a recording is already running on the device, the device is not booted, ffmpeg is not installed (local devices only), or the platform cannot be recorded (tvOS, Chromium and Vega are unsupported).

udid.description: Target device id from `list-devices` (iOS Simulator UDID or Android serial).

timeLimitSeconds.description: Auto-stop cap in seconds (default 180). Set it to slightly more than the interaction you plan to capture. Range: 1 to 600.

trimStatic.description: Default true. Collapse stretches where the screen does not change: the first second of each still stretch is kept, then unchanged frames are dropped until something moves again, so a long recording with brief activity comes back short instead of full of dead air. Set false to keep a faithful real-time recording.

showTouches.description: Default true. Draw an on-screen marker for every tap, swipe, drag, pinch and rotate into the video, so it shows where each interaction landed. Set false to record the raw screen with no overlay.

tools.name: screen-recording-stop
tools.description:
Stop the screen recording started by `screen-recording-start` and retrieve the mp4 video.
Also retrieves the video when the recording already ended on its own (time limit reached, capture process died); call it even after the cap fired.
On a remote (`remote:`) simulator it downloads the mp4.
Use when the interaction being captured is finished, or a tool-result note reminds you a recording is still running.
Returns { video, durationMs, wallClockMs?, trimmedMs?, panelSwitches?, warning? }; video is a downloadable artifact materialized to a local path. When static-frame trimming removed dead air, durationMs is the trimmed video length and wallClockMs/trimmedMs report the real duration and how much was cut. On a foldable simulator the recording follows the panel that shows the UI: panelSwitches counts the panel changes, the video keeps the size of the first panel, and warning is set when argent could not find that panel during the recording.
Fails if no recording (running or finished-but-unretrieved) exists for the given udid.

udid.description: Target device id from `list-devices` (iOS Simulator UDID or Android serial).

tools.name: gesture-tap
tools.description:
Press the device screen (iOS simulator or physical device, Android emulator, or Chromium app) at a point given as fractions of the screen width and height (not pixels): a Down event followed by an Up event at the same spot.
Use when tapping a button, link, or any tappable element on the screen.
Returns { tapped: true, timestampMs }. On physical iOS, reactivated: true = app was re-fronted; re-describe. Fails if the device backend (simulator-server / emulator / Chromium CDP) is unreachable.
Before tapping, take the coordinates from `describe` on every platform (on Chromium it walks the DOM). More information in `argent-device-interact` skill

udid.description: Target device id from `list-devices` (iOS UDID, Android serial, or Chromium id).

x.description: Horizontal position: 0 = left edge, 1 = right edge. Range: 0 to 1.

y.description: Vertical position: 0 = top edge, 1 = bottom edge. Range: 0 to 1.

clickCount.description: Number of taps/clicks dispatched as ONE gesture inside the OS double-tap window (2 = double-tap / double-click), which two separate tap calls cannot guarantee. On physical iOS, higher counts loop single taps, which a double-tap recognizer may pair. Default 1. Range: 1 to 10.

tools.name: chromium-tabs
tools.description:
List and switch the tabs / windows of a Chromium (CDP) app (an Electron app's BrowserWindows or a Chromium browser's tabs), and open or close them.
The active tab is what describe / gesture-tap / screenshot / debugger-evaluate / open-url all operate on, so select a tab before driving it. tabIds (`t1`, `t2`, …) are stable for the session and never reused.
Use when an app exposes multiple windows or tabs and you need to inspect or drive one other than the current page, or to open/close a page during an e2e test.
Returns { tabs: [{ tabId, targetId, title, url, active, label? }] } after the action. Fails if the device is not a Chromium (CDP) device, or the requested tabId/label no longer matches a live tab.

udid.description: Chromium device id from `list-devices` (e.g. `chromium-cdp-9222`).

action.description: list: enumerate tabs/windows. select: make a tab active. new: open a tab and activate it. close: close a tab; if it was active, another live tab becomes active.

tab.description: Target tab for `select` (required) / `close`: a tabId like `t2` or a label. `close` defaults to the active tab.

url.description: `new` only: URL to open (defaults to about:blank).

label.description: `new` only: a memorable label usable interchangeably with the tabId.

tools.name: chromium-cookies
tools.description:
Read and write cookies of a Chromium (CDP) app, HttpOnly cookies included.
`set` needs `name`, `value`, and `url` or `domain`; `delete` needs `name` and `url` or `domain`.
Use when seeding an authenticated session before an e2e test (set the session cookie, then navigate) or asserting cookie state after one.
Returns { cookies, count } for get, or a small status object ({ set } / { deleted } / { cleared }) otherwise. Fails if the device is not a Chromium (CDP) device, or a param that `set` / `delete` needs is missing.

udid.description: Chromium device id from `list-devices` (e.g. `chromium-cdp-9222`).

action.description: get: read cookies. set: create/update a cookie. delete: remove matching cookies. clear: remove ALL browser cookies.

url.description: get: restrict to this URL (defaults to the active page). set/delete: scope the cookie by URL.

domain.description: set/delete: scope the cookie by domain.

expires.description: set: expiry as a Unix timestamp (seconds). Omit for a session cookie.

tools.name: gesture-swipe
tools.description:
Execute a smooth swipe / drag touch gesture between two points on the device (iOS simulator or physical device, or Android emulator). All from/to positions are fractions of screen width/height (not pixels), same as gesture-tap.
Generates interpolated Move events for a natural feel (~60fps).
Swipe up (fromY > toY) to scroll content down.
Use when you need to scroll a list, dismiss a modal, drag an element, or navigate between pages. Not supported on Chromium; use gesture-scroll there instead.
Physical iOS: an edge gesture (back-swipe) needs fromX 0 exactly; durationMs sets drag speed, not time; momentum:false only rests 300ms at the end and does not damp.
Returns { swiped: true, timestampMs }. On physical iOS, reactivated: true = app was re-fronted; re-describe. Fails if the simulator-server / emulator backend is not reachable for the given device.

udid.description: Target device id from `list-devices` (iOS UDID or Android serial).

durationMs.description: Total gesture duration in milliseconds (default 300); the finger stays down this long. Below ~32ms the whole travel lands in one or two frames, which the OS flings as hard as any flick. Maximum: 10000.

momentum.description: Whether the swipe releases with momentum; default true (a natural flinging swipe). false eases the finger into the end point so the OS applies little to no fling and the content stops where the finger lifts: use it when you need a deterministic scroll distance, e.g. in scroll-to-element loops. false needs durationMs >= 150 and is rejected below that; near 150 it can still land short or fling, so keep the default 300.

tools.name: gesture-scroll
tools.description:
Send mouse-wheel events at a point to scroll content in a Chromium app. The anchor x/y and the deltas are fractions of the window (not pixels); x/y match gesture-tap and describe.
Use when content is below/above the fold (describe shows off-screen elements with zero height) or a list needs scrolling. Chromium only: on iOS/Android use gesture-swipe.
Returns { scrolled: true, timestampMs }. Fails if the Chromium CDP session is not reachable for the given device.

udid.description: Target Chromium device id from `list-devices` (chromium-cdp-<port>).

x.description: Anchor x. The wheel events land here; put it over the element you want to scroll. Range: 0 to 1.

deltaX.description: Horizontal scroll distance as a fraction of the window width. Positive reveals content to the right; negative scrolls back left.

deltaY.description: Vertical scroll distance as a fraction of the window height (0.5 = half a window). Positive scrolls down (reveals content below), like rolling a mouse wheel toward you; negative scrolls back up.

durationMs.description: Spread the scroll over this many milliseconds in wheel-event steps (default 300) so scroll handlers fire progressively.

tools.name: gesture-drag
tools.description:
Press the left mouse button at a start point, move to an end point, and release: a desktop mouse drag in a Chromium app, with mouse moves interpolated at ~60fps. All positions are fractions of the window width/height (not pixels), the same space as gesture-tap and describe, except that exactly 1.0 lands one pixel inside the window edge.
Use for slider thumbs, drag-and-drop, text selection, or draggable UI elements. Dragging never scrolls content on desktop; use gesture-scroll for lists/pages. Chromium only: on iOS/Android use gesture-swipe.
Returns { dragged: true, timestampMs }. Fails if the Chromium CDP session is not reachable for the given device.

udid.description: Target Chromium device id from `list-devices` (chromium-cdp-<port>).

durationMs.description: Total drag duration in milliseconds (default 300); the button stays down this long. Maximum: 10000.

momentum.description: Whether the drag releases with momentum; default true (a constant-speed drag). false decelerates into the release point, so an app that derives a fling from the release velocity (carousels, drag libraries) applies little to no momentum: use it when the drag must stop where it was aimed. Under ~100ms durationMs some fling survives; keep the default 300 when the fling must be fully suppressed.

tools.name: gesture-custom
tools.description:
Send a sequence of touch events for complex gestures.
Use for: long press, drag-and-drop, custom scroll, pinch (second touch point).
For simple taps use the gesture-tap tool. For straight-line scrolling use the gesture-swipe tool.
For pinch gestures use gesture-pinch. For rotation gestures use gesture-rotate.
All x/y values are fractions of the screen width/height (not pixels).
Physical iOS: a Down, any Moves, then an Up; x2/y2 adds a second finger. A plain Down then Up: same point = press-hold, other point = drag (Up delayMs = rest before the move); one Move at the Down point between them = long-press pickup (Move delayMs = hold, Up delayMs = move time). Any other train plays as timed paths, each event waiting its delayMs, and needs the app drawn in portrait.
Returns { events: number } with the total count of events dispatched. On physical iOS, reactivated: true = app was re-fronted; re-describe. Fails if the target device is not booted or an event type is invalid.

Example long-press at center:
  [{"type":"Down","x":0.5,"y":0.5},{"type":"Up","x":0.5,"y":0.5,"delayMs":800}]

Example pick up a list item with a long press, then drag it up:
  [{"type":"Down","x":0.5,"y":0.6},{"type":"Move","x":0.5,"y":0.6,"delayMs":800},{"type":"Up","x":0.5,"y":0.3,"delayMs":500}]

Example smooth scroll down:
  [{"type":"Down","x":0.5,"y":0.7},
   {"type":"Move","x":0.5,"y":0.6},{"type":"Move","x":0.5,"y":0.5},{"type":"Move","x":0.5,"y":0.4},
   {"type":"Up","x":0.5,"y":0.3}]

Example pinch-to-zoom (with interpolate:10 for smoothness):
  events: [{"type":"Down","x":0.4,"y":0.5,"x2":0.6,"y2":0.5},
           {"type":"Up","x":0.2,"y":0.5,"x2":0.8,"y2":0.5}]
  interpolate: 10

udid.description: Target device id from `list-devices` (iOS UDID or Android serial).

x2.description: Second finger x, for two-finger gestures. Range: 0 to 1.

y2.description: Second finger y, for two-finger gestures. Range: 0 to 1.

delayMs.description: Delay before this event in milliseconds (default 16ms ≈ 60fps)

interpolate.description: Number of Move events to insert between each pair of consecutive events, linearly interpolating both x,y and x2,y2 and splitting the delay evenly, for a smooth gesture. Default: no interpolation.

tools.name: gesture-pinch
tools.description:
Execute a pinch-to-zoom gesture by moving two fingers toward or away from a center point to change the scale of on-screen content. Positions and distances are fractions of the screen (0.0–1.0, not pixels), as in gesture-tap.
startDistance > endDistance = pinch in (zoom out). startDistance < endDistance = pinch out (zoom in).
Typical values: startDistance 0.2, endDistance 0.6 for a zoom-in pinch at screen center.
Use when you need to zoom in or out on a map, image, or zoomable view. Returns { pinched: true, timestampMs }. On physical iOS, reactivated: true = app was re-fronted; re-describe. Fails if the simulator-server / emulator backend is not reachable for the given device, or on a physical iPhone when the app is not drawn in portrait.

udid.description: Target device id from `list-devices` (iOS UDID or Android serial).

startDistance.description: Initial distance between the two fingers.

endDistance.description: Final distance between the two fingers.

endCenterX.description: Final horizontal center of the pinch. When set, the centroid drifts linearly from centerX to endCenterX over the gesture (e.g. to keep expanding fingers on-screen near an edge). Omit for a fixed center.

endCenterY.description: Final vertical center of the pinch; drifts from centerY like endCenterX. Omit for a fixed center.

angle.description: Angle in degrees of the axis the fingers lie on: 0 = horizontal (default), 90 = vertical.

tools.name: gesture-rotate
tools.description:
Send a two-finger circular arc gesture to rotate on-screen content by a specified angle. Two fingers are placed opposite each other at a fixed radius from the center, then swept from startAngle to endAngle degrees (endAngle > startAngle = clockwise). All positions and radii are normalized 0.0–1.0 (fractions of screen width/height, not pixels), same coordinate space as gesture-tap and gesture-swipe. Typical values: radius 0.15, startAngle 0, endAngle 90 for a 90° clockwise turn.
Size the orbit with radius, or with radiusX and radiusY together (the pair overrides radius); one half of the pair alone, or none of the three, is rejected. A single radius traces a physical ellipse on a non-square screen (finger separation varies through the turn); for a physically circular orbit, pass radiusX and radiusY with radiusX·width = radiusY·height.
Unlike gesture-pinch which moves fingers linearly to zoom, this orbits fingers in an arc to change orientation.
Use when you need to rotate a map, image picker, or any rotateable UI element. Returns { rotated: true, timestampMs }. On physical iOS, reactivated: true = app was re-fronted; re-describe. Fails if the simulator-server / emulator backend is not reachable for the given device, or on a physical iPhone when the app is not drawn in portrait.

udid.description: Target device id from `list-devices` (iOS UDID or Android serial).

radius.description: Distance from the center to each finger.

radiusX.description: Finger distance along the horizontal axis, as a fraction of screen WIDTH.

radiusY.description: Finger distance along the vertical axis, as a fraction of screen HEIGHT.

startAngle.description: Starting angle in degrees (0 = right, 90 = down)

tools.name: button
tools.description:
Press a device hardware button (iOS simulator or physical device, Android emulator or device).
Supported buttons depend on the platform: buttons not present on the target (e.g. 'back' on iOS, 'actionButton' on Android, 'power' or 'appSwitch' on a physical iPhone) are rejected with a clear error.
Use when you need to trigger hardware button events.
Returns { pressed: buttonName }.
Fails if the device backend is not reachable: the simulator-server for iOS, or `adb` for Android.

udid.description: Target device id from `list-devices` (iOS UDID or Android serial).

tools.name: keyboard
tools.description:
Type text or press special keys on the device (iOS simulator, Android emulator or device, Chromium app, Vega Virtual Device, or Apple TV / Android TV) using keyboard events.
Use when you need to enter text or trigger a named key such as enter, escape, or arrow keys. On Vega and Apple TV / Android TV, prefer the remote tools for D-pad navigation; focus a text field with `tv-remote` first (e.g. a search or login box), then type into it with keyboard.
Tap the field first: with no focus the text is dropped and the call still succeeds.
Returns { typed: string, keys: number }. On physical iOS, reactivated: true = app was re-fronted; re-describe. Fails if an unsupported key name is provided (rejected before anything is sent) or if the device's input backend is not reachable.
A failure is not rolled back. Un-typeable text is rejected mid-string on the iOS simulator and Chromium, leaving the characters before it in the field (Android, Vega and TV targets check the whole string up front). A transport failure partway also leaves the text already sent. On a retry, read the field's actual contents; do not assume it is unchanged.
React Native: after typing, the next tap outside the field may only close the keyboard. If only the keyboard closed, tap again; where the field submits on return, `key: "enter"` avoids the extra tap.

udid.description: Target device id from `list-devices` (iOS UDID, Android serial, Vega serial, or Chromium id).

text.description: Text to type character by character; handles uppercase, digits and common punctuation. Cannot be combined with `key`: to type and then press a key, send two `keyboard` steps in one `run-sequence` ({ text: "hello" } then { key: "enter" }). To type a credential without its plaintext ever entering your context, use a secret placeholder `{{secret:<NAME>}}`, e.g. "{{secret:APP_PASSWORD}}", alone or inside longer text. It is resolved on the machine running the tool-server, from the first source that defines the name: the `ARGENT_SECRET_<NAME>` environment variable, `.argent/secrets.env` in the project, the project's `.env.local` / `.env` (only their `ARGENT_SECRET_`-prefixed keys), then `~/.argent/secrets.env`. Nothing else on the host is reachable. Over a link with the `forward-secrets` flag on, the client's own sources are checked first. The result echoes the placeholder, never the value, and the auto-screenshot after typing is skipped. To submit after a secret, put both steps in ONE `run-sequence`: that keeps the skip covering the Enter, which a second bare `keyboard` call would not. If the secret is not set, the failure lists the available names and the sources it checked; ask the user to add it to one of them (a secrets file applies immediately, an env var needs a restart). NEVER ask the user to paste the secret value into the conversation.

key.description: Named key to press: enter, escape, backspace, tab, space, arrow-up, arrow-down, arrow-left, arrow-right, f1-f12. Cannot be combined with `text`; to do both, send two `keyboard` steps in one `run-sequence`. Not supported on Apple TV / Android TV; move focus with `tv-remote` (up/down/left/right) instead. Physical iOS: only `enter` and `backspace`.

delayMs.description: Delay in ms between key presses (default 50). Ignored on Android phones/tablets, Vega, Apple TV / Android TV and physical iOS, which type the whole string in one shot or at their own cadence.

tools.name: paste
tools.description:
Set the DEVICE clipboard to `text`, then trigger the platform's paste shortcut to paste it into the focused field (iOS simulator, Android emulator).
Do NOT use this in place of `keyboard`. `keyboard` types as a user would and is the default for all text entry; call this only where a real user would paste: a 2FA/OTP code copied from another app, a long link or token, or when testing the app's own paste handling.
Tap the field first so it has focus. Returns { pasted: true }, plus via: "keyboard" when a secret was typed instead of pasted. Fails on a TV target, when the device clipboard cannot be set, when a secret that has to be typed holds a character that cannot be typed, or when the simulator-server build lacks clipboard support.

udid.description: Target device id from `list-devices` (iOS simulator UDID or Android emulator serial).

text.description: Text to put on the device clipboard and paste into the focused field. Supports `{{secret:<NAME>}}` placeholders, resolved on the tool-server from the `ARGENT_SECRET_<NAME>` environment variable or an argent secrets file (the same sources as `keyboard`), so a credential never enters your context and is never echoed back. If the secret is not set, the failure lists the available names and every source it looked in; ask the user to add it there, NEVER ask for the value in the conversation.

tools.name: rotate
tools.description:
Set the device orientation.
Use when testing layout in a different orientation. Re-run `describe` afterwards: frame coordinates change with the orientation.
On an unfolded foldable iOS simulator (the iPhone Duo), the value sets the orientation of the device, not of the UI: `Portrait` gives a landscape UI and `LandscapeLeft` gives a portrait UI. To fold or unfold the device, use `fold`.
Returns { orientation }. Fails on a TV target, or if the target device is not booted.

udid.description: Target device id from `list-devices` (iOS UDID or Android serial).

tools.name: shake
tools.description:
Send a shake gesture to the device (iOS simulator or Android emulator).
Use when you need to trigger anything bound to the shake gesture: iOS's "Undo Typing" / "Redo Typing" prompt in a text field, React Native's developer menu in a debug build, or an app's own shake-to-report handler.
iOS delivers one discrete shake per gesture (the same motion event a physical device raises). Android has no OS-level shake event: the accelerometer is driven through a burst of hard direction changes so app-side detectors fire, and the resting orientation is restored afterwards.
Returns { shaken: true, count }.
Works on local and remote (sim-remote) iOS simulators. Fails on a physical device or a TV: only phone/tablet simulators and emulators are supported.

udid.description: Target device id from `list-devices` (iOS simulator UDID or Android emulator serial).

count.description: How many shake gestures to deliver back-to-back (default 1). Raise it for apps whose shake detector needs sustained motion before it fires. Range: 1 to 10.

tools.name: fold
tools.description:
Move the hinge of a foldable iOS simulator (the iPhone Duo) or Android emulator (a Pixel Fold or generic foldable AVD) to a `posture` or to an `angle`; pass exactly one of the two. The tool returns when the device accepts input again, so the next tap lands.
Use when you must see or test an app in a different posture. `list-devices` marks foldable devices with `foldable: true`. To turn a device without a fold, use `rotate`.
All tools use the active panel (the panel that shows the UI), also after a fold made outside argent. The coordinates and the screenshot size change with the panel. Before you tap, read the element tree in this result or run `describe` again.
iOS: unfolded, the UI is landscape, as on a rotated iPhone. A fold between two angles that are not closed or open can keep the current panel. To change panels, fold to closed or open.
iOS returns { activeScreen, screen: { id, panel, width, height }, posture?, hingeAngle, warning? }. screen names the active panel and gives its size in pixels. posture is set only at 0°, 120° and 180°. warning is set when argent cannot find the active panel, or when the device did not change to the expected panel.
Android returns { posture?, deviceState, hingeAngle?, warning? }. deviceState is the state Android committed (CLOSED, HALF_OPENED, OPENED), and posture is the matching preset. A lock screen the fold raises is dismissed; warning is set when it cannot be, or when a lock screen is showing or the screen is off after the fold. On a generic foldable AVD, closed shows only the left part of the display and describe frames do not match tap coordinates; use a Pixel Fold AVD to test the cover panel.
Fails if the device is not foldable, is a remote simulator or a physical Android device.

udid.description: Target device id from `list-devices` (a foldable iOS simulator UDID or Android emulator serial).

posture.description: Where to move the hinge: `closed` shows the cover panel, `half-open` and `open` show the inner panel.

angle.description: The hinge angle in degrees: 0 = closed, 180 = open. Range: 0 to 180.

tools.name: tv-remote
tools.description:
Press a TV remote / D-pad button (or a whole path of them) on a TV device: Apple TV (tvOS), Android TV (leanback), or Vega (Fire TV).
A TV is navigated with a directional remote, not touch. Use when you need to move focus or press a key on a TV, instead of gesture-tap/swipe (which do not apply on a TV).
Read the screen with `describe` before and after to see where focus landed.
Returns { pressed, count }. Fails on a target that is not a TV, and on the Apple TV simulator for rewind, fastForward, next, previous, volumeUp, volumeDown and mute (its HID stack ignores them); every other button works on all three platforms.

udid.description: Target TV device id from `list-devices` (Apple TV, Android TV, or Vega).

button.description: A single TV-remote button, or a path of them run in one call. Move focus with up/down/left/right, confirm with select, go back with back/menu, exit with home; the media and volume buttons press the matching remote keys. For multi-step navigation pass an array, e.g. ["up","right","right","select"]; strongly prefer this over multiple `tv-remote` calls: the whole path runs in a single call. Max items: 64.

repeat.description: Repeat the whole `button` value this many times (default 1). Compact for long same-button runs, e.g. { button: "down", repeat: 12 }. Range: 1 to 50.

tools.name: run-sequence
tools.description:
Execute several device interaction steps in one call.
Use when every step is known in advance and you do not need to see the screen between steps (e.g. scrolling several times, typing then pressing enter). If a step depends on the result of an earlier one (e.g. a menu item that appears only after a tap), make separate calls instead.
Steps run in order. If a step fails (an error, a tool that is not allowed or not supported on the target, or an await-ui-element that returns success=false), the sequence stops there and later steps do NOT run. Returns { completed, total, steps } with a result or an error for each step that ran, so a stopped sequence returns partial results.
One screenshot and element tree are captured after the whole sequence, not per step: call screenshot separately only for a baseline before it or to see an intermediate step. A `{{secret:...}}` in any step skips that capture, so type a secret and submit it in one sequence.
On a TV target (Apple TV / Android TV / Vega) use tv-remote for remote presses and keyboard for text.

Allowed tools, their args (? = optional) and targets. Positions and distances are 0–1 fractions of the screen (window on Chromium), not pixels; angles are in degrees, durations in ms.
  gesture-tap: x, y, clickCount?  [ios/android/chromium]
  gesture-swipe: fromX, fromY, toX, toY, durationMs?, momentum?  [ios/android]
  gesture-scroll: x, y, deltaX?, deltaY? (signed; positive scrolls down), durationMs?  [chromium]
  gesture-drag: fromX, fromY, toX, toY, durationMs?, momentum?  [chromium]
  gesture-custom: events: [{ type: "Down"|"Move"|"Up", x, y, x2?, y2?, delayMs? }], interpolate?  [ios/android]
  gesture-pinch: centerX, centerY, startDistance, endDistance, endCenterX?, endCenterY?, angle?, durationMs?  [ios/android]
  gesture-rotate: centerX, centerY, startAngle, endAngle, radius (or radiusX + radiusY), durationMs?  [ios/android]
  button: button: "home"|"back"|"power"|"volumeUp"|"volumeDown"|"appSwitch"|"actionButton"  [ios/android]
  keyboard: text? or key? (one per step; key e.g. "enter"), delayMs?  [all; Apple TV / Android TV: text only]
    text may hold {{secret:<NAME>}} placeholders, resolved server-side from ARGENT_SECRET_<NAME> or an argent secrets file (over a forward-secrets link, the client's first), so a credential never enters your context
  paste: text (device clipboard + paste shortcut; only where a user would paste, e.g. an OTP, else keyboard)  [ios sim/android emu]
  rotate: orientation: "Portrait"|"LandscapeLeft"|"LandscapeRight"|"PortraitUpsideDown"  [ios sim/android]
  shake: count?  [ios sim/android emu]
  fold: posture? "closed"|"half-open"|"open", or angle? 0–180, exactly one (later steps land on the new panel, whose coordinates differ)  [foldable ios sim/android emu]
  tv-remote: button (one button, or an array run as a path in one step), repeat?  [apple tv/android tv/vega]
    buttons: up/down/left/right/select/back/home/menu/playPause; rewind/fastForward/next/previous/volumeUp/volumeDown/mute on Android TV and Vega only
  await-ui-element: condition: "exists"|"visible"|"hidden"|"text", selector: { text?, identifier?, role? }, expectedText? (for "text"), textMatch?, timeoutMs?, pollIntervalMs?  [all]

udid.description: Target device id from `list-devices` (iOS UDID, Android serial, Vega serial, or Chromium id), shared across all steps.

tool.description: Tool name: one of the allowed tools listed in the description.

args.description: Tool arguments (excluding udid, which is injected automatically)

delayMs.description: Wait time in ms after this step before the next (default 100)

steps.description: Ordered list of interaction steps to execute sequentially

tools.name: debugger-connect
tools.description:
Connect to a JS runtime CDP debugger.
iOS / Android / Vega: connects to Metro's CDP endpoint on the given port. Chromium: re-uses the page CDP session opened by boot-device.
Returns connection info including port, projectRoot (empty on Chromium and on legacy Metro, e.g. Vega), deviceName, appName, logicalDeviceId, and isNewDebugger, plus a note naming the kept log file when the previous session ended because the app crashed. If already connected, returns the existing connection.
Use when starting a debug session or before calling other debugger-* tools. Fails if the runtime is unreachable (Metro down, or Chromium CDP terminated).

port.description: Metro port. Omit it to use this device's port (8081 by default). Ignored for Chromium, whose CDP port is in device_id. Range: 1 to 65535.

device_id.description: Device id from list-devices: iOS simulator UDID, Android serial, Vega serial (amazon-...), or Chromium device id (chromium-cdp-<port>). Pass this SAME id as device_id to every subsequent debugger-* call to pin them to this device. The returned logicalDeviceId is informational (Metro's own per-connection handle, absent on Vega); you do not switch to it. Forwarding it still resolves here, but the list-devices id is the stable one.

tools.name: debugger-status
tools.description:
Get JS runtime debugger connection status and diagnostic info.
Use when you need to verify connectivity before using other debugger tools. Never fails when the runtime is simply unreachable: it returns a discriminated result instead:
- { status: "connected", ... } with port, projectRoot (empty on Chromium and on legacy Metro, e.g. Vega), deviceName, appName, logicalDeviceId (absent on Vega), isNewDebugger (false on the legacy inspector), connected flag, loadedScripts count, and sourceMapReady (always true: waits for pending source maps before returning).
- { status: "not_connected", connected: false, reason, detail, guidance } (port omitted on Chromium), with reason one of metro_not_running, no_app_connected, device_mismatch, cdp_unreachable, runtime_unresponsive, stale_connection, reconnecting. Follow the guidance field; do not retry in a loop.

port.description: Metro port. Omit it to use this device's port (8081 by default). Ignored for Chromium, whose CDP port is in device_id. Range: 1 to 65535.

device_id.description: Device id from list-devices: the SAME id you passed to debugger-connect (iOS simulator UDID, Android serial, Vega serial, or Chromium device id). The logicalDeviceId debugger-connect returns also resolves here, but prefer the stable list-devices id.

tools.name: debugger-evaluate
tools.description:
Execute arbitrary JavaScript in the app's JS runtime via CDP: Hermes on iOS / Android / Vega, V8 on Chromium.
Returns the result serialized by value as JSON, with deviceName, appName, and logicalDeviceId. Use when you need to read app state, including localStorage and sessionStorage on Chromium, call app functions, or test logic at runtime. Cyclic objects, which many RN runtime values are (fiber nodes, navigation refs, global), fail with a serialization error. Fails if the expression throws or the runtime is not connected.

port.description: Metro port. Omit it to use this device's port (8081 by default). Ignored for Chromium, whose CDP port is in device_id. Range: 1 to 65535.

device_id.description: Device id from list-devices: the SAME id you passed to debugger-connect (iOS simulator UDID, Android serial, Vega serial, or Chromium device id). The logicalDeviceId debugger-connect returns also resolves here, but prefer the stable list-devices id.

expression.description: JavaScript expression to evaluate in the app runtime

tools.name: debugger-reload-metro
tools.description:
Restart the Metro JS bundle in the connected React Native app without restarting the native process.
Use when you want to apply code changes or reset JS state. Returns { reloaded, port, method (cdp or http), deviceName, appName, logicalDeviceId }. Fails if Metro is not running on the given port.

port.description: Metro port. Omit it to use this device's port (8081 by default). Ignored for Chromium, whose CDP port is in device_id. Range: 1 to 65535.

device_id.description: Device id from list-devices: the SAME id you passed to debugger-connect (iOS simulator UDID or Android serial).

tools.name: debugger-component-tree
tools.description:
Fetch the current screen of a running React Native app as a compact tree of React components.
Each on-screen component is listed with its name, its text (or accessibilityLabel when it has no
text), [testID=…] and normalized (tap: x,y) centre in [0,1] (fractions of the screen, not pixels).
Full-screen transparent wrappers and implementation-detail components are pruned. Wrappers the size
of their parent are pruned too, so a missing name proves nothing: check with debugger-inspect-element.

Use when you need what describe does not show: a testID for a selector (on Android, describe omits
the testID of a view that has no label and is not tappable), or the component names and nesting
behind the screen before editing code. To find what to tap, use describe.

On an iOS simulator with a landscape UI (a rotated device, or an unfolded foldable), the tap
coordinates are on the screen's axes, which the gesture tools use.
Returns a compact text tree; call again after navigation. Fails if the Metro debugger is not connected.

port.description: Metro port. Omit it to use this device's port (8081 by default). Ignored for Chromium, whose CDP port is in device_id. Range: 1 to 65535.

device_id.description: Device id from list-devices: the SAME id you passed to debugger-connect (iOS simulator UDID or Android serial).

udid.description: iOS simulator UDID from list-devices. Pass it when device_id is a logicalDeviceId (two or more devices share one Metro), so that the tap coordinates of a landscape UI are on the screen's axes. Give the UDID of the simulator that shows the app.

onScreenOnly.description: When true, only components visible on screen are returned. Set to false to include all mounted components, including those scrolled off-screen, e.g. to understand the full page structure. Default: true.

maxNodes.description: Maximum total nodes to include. When exceeded, intermediate single-child wrapper chains are collapsed to preserve both root structure and leaf elements. Default: no limit.

includeSkipped.description: When true, appends a summary of all filtered components: total fiber count and skip counts by component name and by filter. Default: false.

tools.name: debugger-inspect-element
tools.description:
Inspect the React component hierarchy at a screen coordinate (x, y).
Returns components from the tapped element upward through its parent hierarchy,
each with its source file:line and a code fragment.
The first items (lowest indices) are the most specific: the exact component under
the tap point and its direct parents. Higher indices are broader context (page, navigator).
Use when you need the source file and line for a component at a tap coordinate. Fails if the app is not connected or the coordinate is outside the screen.

port.description: Metro port. Omit it to use this device's port (8081 by default). Ignored for Chromium, whose CDP port is in device_id. Range: 1 to 65535.

device_id.description: Device id from list-devices: the SAME id you passed to debugger-connect (iOS simulator UDID or Android serial).

x.description: X coordinate on device screen, in logical pixels (not normalized 0–1)

y.description: Y coordinate on device screen, in logical pixels (not normalized 0–1)

contextLines.description: Lines of source context to include around the component definition. Default: 3.

resolveSourceMaps.description: When true, resolves bundled frame locations to original source files via Metro symbolication and includes a code fragment. When false, returns the raw bundled frame info (file, line, column) without a code fragment. Default: true.

maxItems.description: Maximum number of hierarchy items to return, most specific first. The default covers all app-specific code; increase to 70+ to also see the navigation/screen structure. Default: 35.

includeSkipped.description: When true, items that would normally be filtered are kept in the response with skipped=true and a skipReason. Default: false.

tools.name: debugger-log-registry
tools.description:
Get a summary of all console logs captured from the app's JS runtime.
Returns the log file path, entry counts by level, and message clusters (grouped by similarity). Works against Hermes (iOS / Android / Vega) and V8 (Chromium).
Use when investigating warnings, errors, or unexpected output. Call this first for an overview, then Grep the returned file for details; never Read it whole, it can hold 50,000 lines. Returns empty stats if no log data has been captured yet, but check { note }, which is present only when the stats are empty BECAUSE the previous debugger session ended: torn down (its log file deleted) or cut off by an app crash (its log file kept at the path the note names). Without that note, empty means the app has logged nothing.
When the debugger cannot be reached, it returns { status: "not_connected", reason, detail, guidance } with NO log file. Follow the guidance (do not retry in a loop). Grep a log file in this state only when a { note } names one kept from before the app crashed. A "connected" result's stats may come from a session whose socket has since died. Use debugger-status, not this tool, to judge debugger health.

port.description: Metro port. Omit it to use this device's port (8081 by default). Ignored for Chromium, whose CDP port is in device_id. Range: 1 to 65535.

device_id.description: Device id from list-devices: the SAME id you passed to debugger-connect (iOS simulator UDID, Android serial, Vega serial, or Chromium device id). The logicalDeviceId debugger-connect returns also resolves here, but prefer the stable list-devices id.

tools.name: view-network-logs
tools.description:
Retrieve captured network (HTTP) requests from the running app.
Returns a paginated list of requests with method, URL, status, resource type, size, and duration.
A size with "~" is estimated from the body's length in characters; on React Native, "→ <url>" is the final URL after a redirect.
Pass an entry's requestId to view-network-request-details for full details.
On React Native (iOS / Android / Vega) an interceptor injected into the JS runtime records each request once, from XMLHttpRequest (axios included), React Native's fetch, Expo's fetch, and, in a Metro development build, a fetch library that sends through React Native's network module itself, such as react-native-fetch-api. Capture starts at the first network-tool call; a reload clears it. On Chromium it reads the CDP Network domain of the active tab (all request types).
Use when inspecting outbound HTTP traffic or debugging API calls in the running app.
Fails if the app is not connected (RN) or the device is not reachable (Chromium).

port.description: Metro port. Omit it to use this device's port (8081 by default). Ignored for Chromium, whose CDP port is in device_id. Range: 1 to 65535.

device_id.description: Device id from list-devices (iOS simulator UDID or Android serial), the same id used with debugger-connect.

pageIndex.description: Page index (0-based) or "latest" for the most recent page. Each page contains up to 50 entries. Default: "latest". Minimum: 0.

tools.name: view-network-request-details
tools.description:
Get full details of a specific network request by its requestId.
Returns request/response headers (sensitive headers redacted), status, timing, the request body, and optionally the response body.
Request and response bodies over 1000 chars are cut to 1000 under a "[TRUNCATED: ...]" line that gives the full size; a binary response body is omitted. Use when you need headers, body, or timing for a specific request after listing logs.
Returns an error message string if the requestId is not found.

port.description: Metro port. Omit it to use this device's port (8081 by default). Ignored for Chromium, whose CDP port is in device_id. Range: 1 to 65535.

device_id.description: Device id from list-devices (iOS simulator UDID or Android serial), the same id used with debugger-connect. An android- ID needs no debugger connection.

requestId.description: The requestId from view-network-logs, or an android- ID from native-network-logs.

includeBody.description: Whether to include the response body (if captured). Default: true.

tools.name: describe
tools.description:
Get the accessibility / DOM element tree for the current screen.
Use when you need element frames or labels and have no fresh tree: most interaction tools (not tv-remote or shake) already return one after each action.
On iOS it reads the AXRuntime accessibility service, so it sees whatever is visible, including system dialogs and permission prompts. While a system dialog is visible it returns the dialog's elements (buttons, text); otherwise the foreground app's. On a physical iOS device it covers only the app started with launch-app; to read system dialogs there, launch-app `com.apple.springboard` first.
On Android it reads the tree through Argent's UiAutomation helper, falling back to `uiautomator dump`. On Chromium it walks the DOM over the Chrome DevTools Protocol: every visible element with its ARIA role, accessible name and bounding rect.
On Vega (Fire TV) it reads the on-device automation toolkit; `[focused]`/`[selected]` mark the D-pad cursor, which you move with `tv-remote` (Vega has no touch).
On a TV target (Apple TV / Android TV: a `list-devices` entry with runtimeKind 'tv') it returns the FOCUSED element and the FOCUSABLE elements instead, since a TV UI has no tap coordinates. Move the highlight with `tv-remote`, then call describe again to confirm where focus landed.

Returns `{ description, source }`: `description` renders the tree one line per element, with its role, label/value/id, VoiceOver hint (iOS simulator), interactivity flags and frame. Frames are normalized [0,1] fractions of the screen / window width and height (not pixels); tap an element at the centre of its frame. The tree has no z-order or occlusion information: an element may be covered by an overlay (e.g. a toolbar over list rows), so check a screenshot when a tap lands unexpectedly.
Fails if the tree cannot be read, e.g. on a physical iOS device before launch-app has started an app.

For UIKit properties of a view (class name, accessibilityIdentifier), use native-find-views (iOS simulator only).
For React Native component names, or a testID describe does not list, use debugger-component-tree.

tools.name: await-ui-element
tools.description:
Block until a UI element reaches an expected state or the timeout elapses, so you don't have to poll screenshot/describe yourself. It polls the same tree as `describe`.
Use when the next step needs an element that appears or disappears asynchronously, e.g. after a tap or navigation, or before tapping something that loads late.
Returns { success: boolean, elapsed: number, note?, cause? }. If the condition does not hold by the timeout, it returns success=false, and that is not always a verdict on the condition: `cause` says which it was: `unmet` (the tree was read and the condition was false there), `unreadable` (no trustworthy read, so nothing was judged) or `cancelled`. `note` describes what was seen. Only `unmet` licenses rewriting the check.

udid.description: Target device id from `list-devices` (iOS UDID, Android serial, Vega serial, or Chromium id).

condition.description: What to wait for. `exists`: the selector matches an element anywhere in the tree. `visible`: it matches one with a non-zero on-screen frame. `hidden`: it matches nothing, or only a zero-area element (e.g. a spinner that went away). `text`: the first visible match in reading order (topmost, then leftmost; the first match overall if none is visible) contains expectedText, or equals it with textMatch `equals`. role.description: Case-insensitive substring of the element's role (e.g. AXButton, button, TextView).

selector.description: Element to match. Give at least one field; every given field must match.

expectedText.description: Required for condition `text`: the string the checked match must contain or equal (see `textMatch`).

textMatch.description: For condition `text`: how expectedText is compared. `contains` (default) is a case-insensitive substring; `equals` is a case-insensitive full-string match.

bundleId.description: iOS app bundle id, passed to the describe fallback (see `describe`). Ignored on every other platform, including physical iOS.

pollIntervalMs.description: How often to re-check the tree (default 400). Range: 50 to 5000.

tools.description:
Block until the screen has rendered content and stopped changing, or the timeout elapses. It polls the same element tree as `describe`.
Use when a launch or navigation must finish rendering before a screenshot or tap.

tools.description:

Use when you need to profile a user interaction.
On an iOS simulator or Android device, also call native-profiler-start in the same message with the same device_id, unless the user has said no to native profiling. profiler-combined-report then correlates the two.
After starting, ask the user to perform the interaction to profile, then call react-profiler-stop.
Returns { started_at, startedAtEpochMs, hermes_version, detected_architecture }. On Android, a warning names the apps with native network capture on (started by native-network-logs): their timings in the profile can differ. If a session is already running, returns { already_running: true, mine, owner, … } instead, without clobbering its data, unless it is another tool-server's stale run, has no owner record, or is a lost run of this tool-server: start replaces those. mine: true means this tool-server started the run: if it is yours, call react-profiler-stop. With stale: true it may be another agent's: follow the note. Otherwise, BEFORE OVERTAKING with { force: true }, ask the user for approval first, as how_to_reclaim explains. A start that replaces a run reports it in took_over.

tools.name: react-profiler-stop
tools.description:
Stop CPU profiling and collect the cpuProfile + React commit tree.
Stores the results for react-profiler-analyze, profiler-commit-query and profiler-cpu-query.
Call react-profiler-start first, then exercise the app, then call this.
Returns { duration_ms, sample_count, fiber_renders_captured, total_react_commits, hot_commit_indices, react_render_ms, react_render_share_pct, react_render_peak_1s_pct }.

render cascades, root cause identification, and a top components table.
Raw profiling data is saved to disk with a unique session timestamp for later reload via profiler-load.
After presenting the report, ask the user whether to investigate further (drill-down with
profiler-cpu-query / profiler-commit-query) or implement fixes and re-profile for comparison.

tools.description:
Inspect the React fiber tree and return a JSON representation of the component hierarchy.

tools.name: native-profiler-start
tools.description:
Start native profiling on a booted device. iOS: Instruments via xctrace (CPU, hangs, memory leaks). Android: Perfetto (CPU, jank, RSS-growth weak signal).
After starting, let the user interact with the app, then call native-profiler-stop.
Use when you want to capture native CPU, hang, and memory data for a running app.
Returns { status, pid, traceFile } confirming the recording has started. On Android, a warning names the apps with native network capture on (started by native-network-logs): their timings in the profile can differ.

When true, cold-launches the app under the profiler with Malloc Stack Logging enabled so memory leaks carry an allocation backtrace (responsible frame + library). Trade-offs: this RESTARTS the app (current state is lost), adds memory/CPU overhead, and makes the app noticeably slow to launch, so leave it off for pure CPU/hang profiling. Rejected up front under the all-processes capture (used where Xcode's `--device` recording is broken, or forced with ARGENT_IOS_CAPTURE=all-processes), which cannot cold-launch and records no leaks.

tools.name: native-profiler-stop
tools.description:
Stop native profiling and export trace data: CPU, hangs, and leaks XML from xctrace on iOS; the Perfetto .pftrace on Android.
Use when the user has finished the interaction to profile and you need to export the trace.
Returns { traceFile, exportedFiles, exportDiagnostics? }; traceFile is the raw trace bundle and exportedFiles the exports, all downloadable artifacts materialized to local paths.

device_id.description: Target device id from `list-devices` (iOS UDID or Android serial).

tools.name: native-profiler-analyze
tools.description:
Analyze exported native trace data and return a markdown report with severity indicators, tables, and actionable suggestions.
iOS: CPU time profile, UI hangs, and memory leaks from the exported XML files.
Android: CPU hotspots, UI hangs with jank reason + main-thread state breakdown, GC annotation, and an RSS-growth weak signal from the Perfetto .pftrace.
After presenting the report, ask the user whether to investigate further (drill-down with
profiler-stack-query for hang stacks, CPU context, leak details) or implement fixes and re-profile.
Use when you need to interpret a completed native profiling recording.
Fails if native-profiler-stop has not been called first to export trace data.

device_id.description: Target device id from `list-devices` (iOS UDID or Android serial).

tools.name: profiler-cpu-query
tools.description:
Query Hermes CPU profile data with targeted modes for iterative investigation.
Modes:
- top_functions: Global CPU hotspots ranked by self-time. Optional time_window_ms to filter.
- time_window: CPU breakdown for time_window_ms (e.g. during a slow commit or hang).
- call_tree: For a given function_name, show its callees, and its callers with include_callers.
- component_cpu: For a given component_name, aggregate CPU activity across its stored commits.
In top_functions and time_window, self-times are the summed sampling intervals of the samples that
landed in the window, so they measure sampled coverage rather than the window's width and do not
change if you widen the query. Their tables state how many samples they cover and how much was idle.
Each row is one call path, so a function can have several rows and top_n counts rows.
Use when investigating JS CPU hotspots or correlating CPU cost with specific components.
Returns a markdown table of CPU hotspots, call tree, or per-component CPU breakdown.
Fails if no CPU profile is stored; run react-profiler-stop (and ideally react-profiler-analyze) first.

port.description: Metro port. Omit it to use this device's port (8081 by default). Ignored for Chromium, whose CDP port is in device_id. Range: 1 to 65535.

device_id.description: Device logicalDeviceId from debugger-connect (iOS simulator UDID or Android logicalDeviceId).

mode.description: Query mode; see Modes in the tool description.

time_window_ms.description: Time window in ms since profiling started, the same clock profiler-commit-query prints

top_n.description: Number of results to return. Default: 15. Must be greater than 0.

include_callers.description: Also show callers of the function. Default: false.

react_only.description: top_functions and time_window: list only React component functions (PascalCase names). Default: false.

tools.name: profiler-commit-query
tools.description:
Query React commit data for iterative investigation of render performance.
Modes:
- by_component: All commits where component_name rendered, with causes and durations.
- by_time_range: What happened in time_range_ms.
- by_index: Full detail dump of the commit at commit_index (all components, props changed, parent cascade).
- cascade_tree: Parent-child cascade tree for the commit at commit_index, showing who triggered whom.
- render_counts: Re-render count, rate and self time per component over ALL commits, including those under 16ms that the other modes cannot see. Library components included.
Use when drilling into specific components or time windows after react-profiler-analyze.
Returns a markdown table or tree of commit data matching the requested mode.
Fails if react-profiler-stop has not been called.

port.description: Metro port. Omit it to use this device's port (8081 by default). Ignored for Chromium, whose CDP port is in device_id. Range: 1 to 65535.

device_id.description: Device logicalDeviceId from debugger-connect (iOS simulator UDID or Android logicalDeviceId).

mode.description: Query mode; see Modes in the tool description.

component_name.description: Component name; optional for render_counts, which it narrows to one component

time_range_ms.description: Time range in ms since profiling started, the clock this tool prints

top_n.description: Max results to return. Defaults to 20 for by_component / by_time_range, which count commits, and render_counts, which counts components. by_index counts individual fibers and returns all of them unless this is set; a small cap there can show less than the analyze report it is meant to expand on. Must be greater than 0.

tools.name: profiler-stack-query
tools.description:
Query native profiler trace data for iterative investigation of native performance.
Modes:
- hang_stacks: Full CPU context during a specific hang (by hang_index).
- function_callers: Who calls function_name and what it calls.
- thread_breakdown: CPU time split by thread, optionally filtered.
- leak_stacks: Memory leak details (iOS only), optionally filtered by object_type.
Use when drilling into native hang stacks, thread CPU breakdown, or memory leaks after native-profiler-analyze.
Returns a markdown report with native call stacks, thread weights, or leak details for the selected mode.
Fails if native-profiler-stop → native-profiler-analyze has not been run or no parsed trace data is in memory.

mode.description: Query mode; see Modes in the tool description.

thread.description: Thread filter. thread_breakdown: case-insensitive substring match. function_callers: exact raw thread name (e.g. ".blueskyweb.app"), or "main" for the UI thread; omit to search ALL threads (each result is tagged with its thread). Run thread_breakdown first to see the exact raw names.

tools.name: profiler-combined-report
tools.description:
Generate a cross-correlated report combining React Profiler and native profiler data.
Maps native hangs to React commits using wall-clock time alignment.
Call this tool when both profilers were run in parallel on the same session.
Returns a markdown report correlating hangs with React commits, memory leaks, and investigation hints.
Fails if either react-profiler-analyze or native-profiler-analyze has not been called first, or if the session stored no React commits.

port.description: Metro port. Omit it to use this device's port (8081 by default). Ignored for Chromium, whose CDP port is in device_id. Range: 1 to 65535.

device_id.description: iOS Simulator/device UDID or Android serial

tools.name: profiler-load
tools.description:
Fetch and restore a profiling session that react-profiler-stop or native-profiler-stop saved to disk, so the query tools (profiler-cpu-query, profiler-commit-query, profiler-stack-query) can read it.
Use when you need to revisit past session data without capturing a new recording.
Modes:
- list: Show all available profiling sessions in the project's debug directory.
- load_react: Load a React profiler session (CPU profile + commit tree) into memory. Requires session_id.
- load_native: Load a native profiler session (xctrace XML on iOS, .pftrace on Android). Requires session_id.
Loading replaces the session in memory for this device_id (and Metro port, for React): the one the query tools and react-profiler-analyze read. The replaced session stays on disk; load it again by its session_id.
Returns a summary of the loaded session or a session list for the list mode.
Fails if the session_id is not found or the session's trace files are missing from disk.

tools.name: native-network-logs
tools.description:
Retrieve network requests captured at the native level: NSURLProtocol on iOS, OkHttp on Android.
Use when inspecting native-level HTTP traffic that view-network-logs cannot see: requests that never pass through JS XMLHttpRequest or fetch.
On iOS it sees URLSession requests (default and ephemeral session configurations, and URLSession.shared) from native modules and Swift/Objective-C code. It does not see background URLSession transfers, WKWebView, Network.framework, or HTTP stacks that bypass URLSession (e.g. Flutter), so an empty result does not mean the app sent nothing. Capture starts at the first call, so the first call is usually empty: repeat the action, then call again.
On iOS: returns { status, count, events } where each event contains URL, method, status code, headers, and timing.
If status is restart_required: follow the message (usually restart-app), then retry. If status is service_stale: the app is already injected, so restarting it cannot help. Restart the tool-server (`argent server stop && argent server start --detach`) and retry. If the same status comes back after that restart, stop restarting: follow the message, which names the terminal fallback. If status is connect_pending: the app is injected and still connecting. Do not restart it, wait a few seconds and retry. If status is init_failed: follow the message (re-boot the simulator) rather than retrying.
On a device whose devtools agent argent attached to rather than armed itself, a not-connected app fails with `NATIVE_DEVTOOLS_NOT_CONNECTED` instead of a status, and no restart on argent's side fixes it. An Apple system app is rejected outright (terminal: never retry it).
On Android: needs a debuggable build. The first call starts capture and usually returns armed: false. Call it again every few seconds until armed is true, then repeat the action whose requests you need: earlier requests are not captured.
Capture also misses a request already in flight at the attach and requests from clients other than OkHttp (e.g. HttpURLConnection, Cronet); an app whose OkHttp is fully minified reports capture unavailable.
Returns { status, header, armed, capture, captureDetail, count, total, requests }. When capture is active, captureDetail and the header can say that only some requests are captured: then an empty or short list does not mean the app sent nothing. Pass a request's ID (android-3f9a-12) to view-network-request-details for its headers, redirects and bodies.
Capture can slow the app. It stays on, and launch-app and restart-app attach it to each new process, until a call with stop: true turns it off for this app (stop-all-simulator-servers for the device also does); restart-app then starts the app without the agent. stop: true returns { status, stopped, message }, where stopped is false when capture was not on for the app. On iOS stop: true fails: capture there ends only when stop-all-simulator-servers stops this device's services and the app restarts.
When status is not_attachable, use view-network-logs and do not retry.

bundleId.description: App bundle ID on iOS or package name on Android

port.description: Android only: the app's Metro port, whose requests are left out of the listing. Omit it to use this device's port, 8081 by default. Range: 1 to 65535.
