clear.description: Clear the log after reading. On Android, the IDs of cleared requests still work in view-network-request-details. Default: false.

stop.description: Android only: turn native capture off for this app instead of listing. Other apps keep theirs.

tools.name: native-find-views
tools.description:
Search for specific UIViews in the running app by class name, accessibility identifier, accessibility label, tag or React Native nativeID; at least one of these params is required.

Returns { status: "ok", matches }: the matching views with their frames, properties, optional ancestors and optional children. To tap a view, divide the centre of its screenFrame by the screen size in points, which native-full-hierarchy returns as screen (maxDepth: 1 is enough), and pass the result to gesture-tap. Matches are not filtered for visibility. Before tapping, call native-user-interactable-view-at-point at that centre with skipClasses ["UITextEffectsWindow"]. If it does not return the match or a descendant, check a screenshot.
If status is restart_required: follow the message (usually restart-app), then retry. If status is service_stale: the app is already injected, so restarting it cannot help. Restart the tool-server (`argent server stop && argent server start --detach`) and retry. If the same status comes back after that restart, stop restarting: follow the message, which names the terminal fallback. If status is connect_pending: the app is injected and still connecting. Do not restart it, wait a few seconds and retry. If status is init_failed: follow the message (re-boot the simulator) rather than retrying.
An Apple system app is rejected outright (terminal: never retry it).

tools.name: native-user-interactable-view-at-point
tools.description:
Inspect the deepest UIView at a raw native window point that would actually receive touch input.

Unlike native-view-at-point, this respects userInteractionEnabled and is closer to
UIKit hit-testing semantics.

Use when a tap lands somewhere unexpected or does nothing, to see which control
UIKit would hand the touch to: a transparent overlay swallowing it, a parent
recognizer, a disabled button.

Returns { status: "ok", view }: the hit-test winner with its class name, frames,
identifier, label and layer name, plus its ancestors and subviews as requested.
view is null when no touchable view sits under that point.

To get x and y from a normalized describe frame, multiply its values by the
screen size in points, also when the UI is landscape.
native-full-hierarchy returns that size as screen (pass maxDepth: 1 and fields: ["className"] to keep it small).

If status is restart_required: follow the message (usually restart-app), then retry. If status is service_stale: the app is already injected, so restarting it cannot help. Restart the tool-server (`argent server stop && argent server start --detach`) and retry. If the same status comes back after that restart, stop restarting: follow the message, which names the terminal fallback. If status is connect_pending: the app is injected and still connecting. Do not restart it, wait a few seconds and retry. If status is init_failed: follow the message (re-boot the simulator) rather than retrying.
An Apple system app is rejected outright (terminal: never retry it).

tools.name: stop-simulator-server
tools.description: Stop the transport session for a specific device (iOS simulator / Android: simulator-server process; physical iOS: the on-device runner; Chromium: CDP WebSocket) and free its resources; on a TV target it also reaps that device's TV-control daemons. Use to restart a wedged transport, or when the user is done with one device but wants to keep others running - not just because a task on it finished, since the next task on that device would start cold again. On iOS / Android / TV it deliberately leaves this device's native-devtools, accessibility, profiler and debugger services running - to drain those as well, use stop-all-simulator-servers with `devices`. On CHROMIUM, stopping the transport also ends the JS-runtime debugger session and its captured console history - reconnect with debugger-connect afterwards. Returns { stopped, udid }; `stopped` is false, not an error, when no session is open for the id.

udid.description: Target device id (iOS UDID, Android serial, or Chromium id) whose transport session to stop

tools.name: stop-all-simulator-servers
tools.description:
Stop the services a device owns - simulator-server processes (iOS + Android), native devtools, the iOS accessibility service, TV-control daemons, Chromium CDP sessions, screen recordings, native profiler sessions, Android native network capture (started by native-network-logs), and JS-runtime debugger sessions along with the network inspectors and React profiler sessions that ride on them - freeing their spawned processes, sockets and ports. Call this when the user asks to clean up or ends the session, or when a skill tells you to recycle a device's services mid-flow - not just because a task finished, since the next task reuses these services and would start cold again. To end only the native network capture of one app, call native-network-logs with stop: true instead.
PASS `devices` with the device ids this session used: one tool-server serves every agent, subagent and CLI call using this argent install, and an unscoped call tears down THEIR devices too. Omit `devices` only when a machine-wide cleanup is what you actually want. An EMPTY array stops nothing; it does not ask for the machine-wide sweep.
A JS-runtime debugger session is keyed by the id you called `debugger-connect` with. On a Metro serving two or more devices that id is not a udid or serial - connect refuses those and tells you to re-target with the `logicalDeviceId` it returns - so a scope built from `list-devices` ids cannot reach that session. Pass any such `logicalDeviceId` in `devices` ALONGSIDE the device id.
Returns { stopped }: the URNs of the live services that were shut down; empty means nothing was still running. { unmatched }, present only when a supplied id owns no service here, lists those ids, so a typo or a device NAME passed instead of an id does not read as a clean machine. It is NOT proof the id is wrong: a Vega device you only booted and drove with the remote registers no service and lands here, as does any device this session never started anything on. { left_running } lists the URNs of live debugger sessions (and the network inspectors / React profiler sessions riding on them) whose id no device scope can name; re-call with the id after each URN's `<namespace>:<port>:` prefix to reap them. { aborted: true } means the request was cancelled part-way: the rest was left untouched and `unmatched` / `left_running` were not computed.
Fails if the input has an unknown key (e.g. `udids` instead of `devices`); otherwise it always succeeds, and reaping nothing is a result, not a failure.

devices.description: Ids of the devices THIS session used (iOS UDID / Android serial / Chromium id), to scope the teardown to.

tools.name: stop-metro
tools.description: Stop the Metro bundler process listening on `port`. Use when the user asks to stop Metro or when Metro must be restarted - do not offer it when a task wraps up, since the next task would wait on a cold Metro start. Returns { stopped, port, pids }: stopped=true when it sent SIGTERM to every listening pid it found (or the pid had already exited), stopped=false when it found none. Fails if the port lookup cannot run or times out, if it finds a listener but not the process that owns it, or if it cannot signal a listener it found (e.g. EPERM). On macOS another user's listener is detected only when no other listener on the port is visible, so it can survive stopped=true. This is DESTRUCTIVE: always ask the user for confirmation before calling this tool.

port.description: TCP port Metro is listening on. Default: 8081. Range: 1 to 65535.

tools.name: e2e-start-recording
tools.description:
Start recording a new e2e test, resetting .argent/e2e/<name>.yaml to an empty e2e test and replacing any existing one.
Use when you want to capture a reusable sequence of device interactions for later replay. Load the argent-create-e2e skill first: it holds the polish, audit and replay steps. Not for Apple TV or Android TV.
Returns { message, e2eTestFile, savedTo } and optionally { restarted, discardedSteps } if a live recording of the same e2e test was discarded.
Without a link, it creates that file and fails if the .argent/e2e/ directory cannot be created or the file cannot be written. Over a link (argent link or ARGENT_TOOLS_URL, also to 127.0.0.1), your client writes the file, and `savedTo` is its path on your computer, or null when that write failed.

Several e2e tests can be recorded at once, each keyed by the `name` + `project_root`
that every subsequent recording tool repeats, and one recording's steps never
land in another's file.

After starting, use e2e-add-step to append tool calls. Each step runs LIVE, so
give each concurrent recording its own device and pick a name unique to your
task. Read each step's `message`: it warns when a recorded await-ui-element did
not hold, or may fail once converted to `await:`/`assert:`. A wait nested in a
recorded run-sequence gets no such warning, so read its `toolResult`. For a
standalone e2e test, record a restart-app of the app under test as the FIRST step
(captured as the e2e test's `launch` step); for a reusable fragment, skip that and
pass executionPrerequisite instead. Starting over an existing e2e test replaces the
whole file, including its `requires:` block; pass `requires` to keep it.
Use e2e-add-echo to add labels, and
e2e-add-script to run a local .mjs file and record it as a `script:` step.
Call e2e-finish-recording when done.

To remove or reorder steps, edit the .yaml file after e2e-finish-recording, not
during the recording: over a link, the next recorded step writes over your edit,
and without a link, an edit that renumbers the steps drops their warnings.

name.description: Name for this e2e test (e.g. "settings-explore"): letters, digits, underscore and hyphen only.

project_root.description: Absolute path to the project root directory (the directory that contains or should contain `.argent/e2e/`).

executionPrerequisite.description: Fragments only: the app/device state assumed on entry (e.g. "Settings app open on General page"). Omit it for a standalone e2e test. restart-app has no chromium support, so a chromium e2e test records as a fragment; add the `launch: { chromium: <app path> }` line to the YAML afterward, deleting the executionPrerequisite line if you passed one, since an e2e test that starts with a launch must not declare it.

requires.description: The e2e test's `requires:` block: the targets it supports, ANDed. `platform` is one platform or a list (`ios` also covers a remote simulator); `runtimeKind` is `tv` or `mobile`. Omit it for a test that runs on any target.

tools.name: e2e-add-step
tools.description:
Execute one MCP tool and record its step in the e2e test named by `name` + `project_root`. Use when recording and you want each action run and captured; the recording must already be open.
A coordinate `gesture-tap` records as a portable `tap` selector step; `restart-app` as a `launch`.
Returns { message, stepCount, recorded, savedTo }; `recorded`, not the status, says whether a step was appended. Fails with an error, recording nothing. Call recording tools, including `e2e-add-script`, directly.

name.description: Name of the e2e test being recorded: the one passed to e2e-start-recording.

project_root.description: Absolute path to the project root of the e2e test being recorded: the same value passed to e2e-start-recording.

command.description: MCP tool to execute and record, for example "gesture-tap". Do not pass an e2e test directive or a recording tool. Call e2e-add-script directly for a requested script step.

args.description: Tool arguments as a JSON string, e.g. '{"udid": "ABC", "x": 0.5, "y": 0.3}'. Omit for tools with no arguments.

delayMs.description: Milliseconds to sleep before executing this step during replay. Minimum: 0.

tools.name: e2e-add-echo
tools.description:
Record an echo step in the e2e test named by `name` + `project_root`. Echo steps print a message when the e2e test is replayed, useful as labels between tool calls.
Use when you want to annotate a recorded e2e test with a human-readable label or checkpoint message.
Returns { message, stepCount, savedTo }. Fails if that e2e test has no recording in progress.

name.description: Name of the e2e test being recorded: the one passed to e2e-start-recording.

project_root.description: Absolute path to the project root of the e2e test being recorded: the same value passed to e2e-start-recording.

tools.name: e2e-add-script
tools.description: Run a local .mjs file and record it as a `script:` step in an active e2e test. Use when the user requests a local script in the e2e test, and only then. Call it at the point in the recording where the script must run. Returns `status`, `reason` and `stepCount`. A failed script is not recorded. Check `reason` and the affected state before you retry. Over a link (argent link or ARGENT_TOOLS_URL), the tool refuses the call: record such an e2e test with no link.

name.description: E2E test name passed to e2e-start-recording.

project_root.description: Absolute project root passed to e2e-start-recording.

path.description: Path to the .mjs file, relative to the e2e test YAML. For example: "../../scripts/seed-order.mjs".

timeout.description: Time limit in milliseconds. The default is 30000 and the minimum is 100.

tools.name: e2e-finish-recording
tools.description:
Finish recording the e2e test named by `name` + `project_root`, leaving recordings under any other key untouched. Returns { message, path, executionPrerequisite, steps, summary, e2eTestFile, savedTo } - a summary of all recorded steps plus the final YAML. Use when you have added all desired steps and want to finalize the e2e test file. Fails if that e2e test has no recording in progress.
A warning e2e-add-step raised on a recorded `await-ui-element` is repeated in `summary` as a `warning:` line right below its step, and `message` counts them by kind. Read them before you convert a wait to `await:`/`assert:` or replay the e2e test.
You can still edit the .yaml file directly afterwards to remove or reorder steps.

name.description: Name of the e2e test being recorded: the one passed to e2e-start-recording.

project_root.description: Absolute path to the project root of the e2e test being recorded: the same value passed to e2e-start-recording.

tools.name: e2e-execute
tools.description:
Run a saved YAML e2e test end to end. Use when
asked to replay a recorded path, re-run a QA regression, or check that a known journey still passes; for a
one-off interaction use the gesture tools instead, and to author an e2e test use e2e-start-recording. Pass
exactly one e2e test source: name (under project_root) or e2e_test_path.
Returns a per-step report: the first failure stops the run and the rest report as skipped.
Over a link (argent link or ARGENT_TOOLS_URL), the client uploads the e2e test with the run: fragments,
snapshot baselines and absolute .png/.yaml file arguments its steps use, from under project_root or beside
the e2e test file. The run fails if a step needs any other project file (a script: step, a recording tool,
a nested e2e-execute not called by name with an absolute project_root, a directory, app or output-directory
argument, a file path built from several arguments, a relative path): it stops before the first step and the
error lists each such step. An absolute .png/.yaml argument from anywhere else fails only when its step runs.
Without a link, every step kind runs.

name.description: Name of a saved e2e test to run from `<project_root>/.argent/e2e`, or `.argent/flows` when it is not there (e.g. "settings-explore").

project_root.description: Absolute path to the calling agent's project root: the cwd it is working in, also with e2e_test_path, where the e2e test, its run: siblings, its script: paths and baselines resolve beside the YAML instead. A script still RUNS in this root.

e2e_test_file.description: Path to the e2e test .yaml as readable by the tool-server. Internal: the argent client derives it from project_root and name automatically; leave unset.

e2e_test_path.description: Absolute path to an e2e test .yaml on the client.

device.description: Device id to run against (iOS UDID, Android/Vega serial, Chromium id), as list-devices reports it. Auto-detected when omitted, but only when exactly one booted device matches (optionally narrowed by `platform` and the e2e test's `requires:` block); with several booted the run fails and lists them, so pass this explicitly whenever more than one device is up.

platform.description: Restrict auto-detection to this platform when several devices are booted. `ios` selects local simulators only; `ios-remote` selects a remote one. `chromium` with no `device` also makes the runner boot an Electron instance for a standalone e2e test from its `launch` step's chromium value and tear it down after the run, with no fallback to auto-detection (a single-key `launch: { chromium: … }` map, or a `requires:` block that allows only chromium, does this on its own; a fragment, or a launch map without a `chromium` key, is still auto-detected). That value must be an Electron app path on the tool-server host: the bare-string `launch:` the recorder writes holds a bundle id, which fails the run with `Electron boot: path does not exist`, so first edit it to `{ chromium: <app path> }`.

updateBaselines.description: Write/refresh screenshot baselines for `snapshot` steps instead of diffing against them, also in the e2e tests that tool: e2e-execute steps run, unless such a step sets updateBaselines itself. Over a link, the client writes the new baselines when the run ends.

prerequisiteAcknowledged.description: Set to true to confirm the execution prerequisite has been met. Required when a fragment defines an executionPrerequisite: without it, the call runs no step and returns the prerequisite text. Not a dry run: an e2e test with no prerequisite runs in full. To read a prerequisite without running, read executionPrerequisite in the YAML file.

tools.name: update-argent
tools.description: Apply a pending Argent update. Call this only when the user has explicitly consented in this conversation to updating Argent, e.g. after an update notification reports a new version. Returns { message } with the update status, version info, and whether the tool server restarts. Fails if no update is available or an update is already in progress.

target.description: Which install to update. 'auto' (default) updates the install serving this session: the global PATH install or this project's local devDependency, whichever this server runs from. Pass 'global' / 'local' to force one, or 'both' when the user has both and wants each updated.

tools.name: dismiss-update
tools.description: Postpone the Argent update reminder, on every tool-server on this machine, when the user wants it later or tomorrow, wants it stopped, or never wants it (87600 hours). Installs nothing. A memory or a reminder of your own does not change it. Returns { message, remindersResumeAt, persisted, pendingVersion }: tell the user when reminders resume, and if persisted is false, that it did not fully hold.

hours.description: Hours until reminders resume: 168 is a week, 87600 is the longest, 0 turns them back on. Minimum: 0.
